Also test serialize with null object (allowed, should write null). According to serialize(Serializable obj, OutputStream) will write obj (which can be null) fine. So we can deserialize back and get null.

Test serialize with null OutputStream throws IllegalArgumentException.

Test deserialize with null InputStream throws IllegalArgumentException.

Test deserialize with empty byte array leads to EOFException wrapped in SerializationException.

Test clone with null returns null.

Test clone with valid object returns equal but not same reference.

Test that ClassLoaderAwareObjectInputStream resolves class using custom classloader; maybe test with inner class loaded by a custom loader? Could be complex; we can test that clone works for class loaded by custom loader (same as default). Might be not needed.

Test that serialize(byte[]) returns non-empty for non-null object.

Edge: large object, but not needed.

But we can also use @Test(expected=...) for exception.

We'll create a simple Serializable class: SimpleBean implements Serializable with fields int x, String s, equals and hashCode.

Also a non-serializable inner class: NotSerializable.

A bean with non-serializable field: BadBean implements Serializable with NotSerializable field.

- testCloneNullReturnsNull
- testCloneSimpleObject
- testCloneWithNonSerializableFieldThrowsException

- testSerializeToStreamAndDeserializeBack (using ByteArrayOutputStream and deserialize(InputStream))
